outputs: Generated news articles of ~500 words based on news title prompts
Approximately 500‑word news articles generated from news‑title prompts
The paper generates news-like texts using neural language models based on article titles as prompts, producing 500-word articles for analysis in authorship attribution tasks.

methods: binary classification (human vs. machine) using fine‑tuned RoBERTa

changes_made.explanation: Removed all metadata as the paper does NOT use LLMs as judges. The mentioned models are used for classification/detection tasks, not for evaluating NLG outputs as judges.
No human evaluation was conducted in this paper - only linguistic analysis and automated classification

overall_notes: This paper focuses on authorship attribution for neural text generation rather than evaluating NLG quality. The main contributions are around detecting which model generated text and distinguishing human vs machine text. The paper uses linguistic features and classification metrics (F1) for evaluation rather than traditional NLG metrics like BLEU/ROUGE.
